This implies that Doxepin may influence the function of Chrm2, which in turn could modulate the activity of Chrm4. The integration of these pathways suggests that Doxepin may act through a receptor-mediated mechanism, where it interacts with Chrm2, which is part of a broader network of G-protein coupled receptors, ultimately affecting Chrm4. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Doxepin and Chrm4, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
